one_line_reason: Abundant human RCT and meta-analysis evidence exists on oral D-mannose for recurrent UTI prevention, the exact outcome it is marketed for, but recent large meta-analyses directly contradict earlier positive ones -- worth central re-verification.

selected.population: adults and non-adults with recurrent UTI risk (network meta-analysis, 50 RCTs, 10,495 subjects, 14 interventions)
selected.intervention: oral D-mannose vs placebo (among 14 compared non-antibiotic interventions)
selected.why_selected: Largest and most recent network meta-analysis in the shortlist; found D-mannose had the strongest UTI-incidence reduction (RR 0.34) among all 14 interventions compared

selected.population: women (97.6%) at high risk for recurrent UTI (6 RCTs, 1,167 participants)
selected.intervention: oral D-mannose vs no intervention or standard antibiotic therapy
selected.why_selected: The most recent (2025) meta-analysis directly contradicts 39095666: found D-mannose was NOT associated with reduced recurrent UTI versus control or antibiotics, including in postmenopausal women -- this conflict is the central reason to flag D-mannose for deep verification

selected.population: women 18+ in the community with a history of recurrent UTI (99 UK primary care centers, 232 randomized)
selected.intervention: D-mannose powder 2 g/day, oral, 6 months vs matched placebo powder
selected.primary_outcome: proportion of women experiencing a medically attended recurrent UTI
selected.why_selected: The largest, most rigorous single primary-care-based placebo-controlled RCT with a clearly stated dose and community (non-secondary-care) population, closely matching real supplement use; the retrieved abstract text is truncated before the result is stated

selected.population: adults with recurrent UTI, including catheter and non-catheter users (systematic review, 8 studies, 6 clinical with 695 individuals)
selected.intervention: oral D-mannose vs control, various doses
selected.dose_as_stated: not stated (earlier pilot studies cited doses of 200 mg up to 2-3 g)
selected.primary_outcome: recurrent UTI incidence and time to recurrence
selected.why_selected: Earlier systematic review reporting D-mannose reduced recurrent UTI incidence and prolonged UTI-free intervals, representative of the positive evidence base that the 2025 meta-analysis (41004704) later contradicted

blockers: Doses across the underlying primary trials range widely (200 mg to 2-3 g/day), and most of the shortlisted meta-analyses do not state a single pooled dose, complicating any label-dose mapping

The evidence is genuinely conflicting across time: earlier reviews (32972899) and a 2025 network meta-analysis (39095666) found significant benefit, while the most recent direct meta-analysis (41004704) found no significant benefit versus control or antibiotics -- central verification should read the full texts and check for overlapping/duplicate trial inclusion across these reviews

excluded_pmids.reason: Cochrane review of D-mannose for UTI prevention/treatment; the retrieved abstract is largely background/methods (mechanism, early pilot dose ranges) without a stated pooled result, so no extractable finding beyond what 32972899/41004704/39095666 already provide
Meta-analysis of D-mannose vs other agents for recurrent UTI in adult women; the retrieved abstract is truncated before any result is stated

General review of 8 different non-antibiotic UTI approaches (cranberry, Canephron N, probiotics, NSAIDs, D-mannose, estrogens, vitamins, immunotherapy) pooled together; no D-mannose-specific result isolated

Meta-analysis primarily of long-term antibiotics for recurrent UTI in older adults; D-mannose appears only as the comparator in one of three included trials (94 patients), not the focus of this review

Three-arm RCT (hydration vs D-mannose vs antibiotic prophylaxis); the retrieved abstract is truncated before stating the D-mannose-specific comparison to hydration, only that antibiotics had the lowest incidence
Tests a 5-component blend (D-mannose, propolis-quercetin, Bacillus coagulans, hyaluronic acid, chondroitin sulfate) with/without fosfomycin; combination product, not isolated D-mannose

Topical wound-healing study applying D-mannose plus calcium propionate powder directly to surgical wounds; unrelated exposure route (topical) and combination, and not the UTI-prevention outcome D-mannose is marketed for
D-mannose plus proanthocyanidins vs proanthocyanidins alone in de novo kidney transplant recipients; combination product in a small, specific clinical transplant population
